comparison.objective: Adjust and lock damping until repeated axis impacts stop safely, versus fit a rubber stopper at least 12 mm onto a glass tube without unsafe leverage.
comparison.physical_skill: Both use bimanual stabilization and controlled rotation. Candidate additionally requires recessed hex-key insertion, captive-setscrew loosening/relocking, collar tuning, witness torque, and iterative interpretation of impacts; PR-793 requires coaxial stopper seating and simultaneous twist-and-push insertion while gripping close below fragile glass.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate succeeds after two non-bottoming, non-overloading stops with no excessive rebound or setting drift. PR-793 succeeds when the stopper is ≥12 mm down and released, with zero credit if it was worked while the tube lacked a close supporting grip.
comparison.reason: This is the closest mechanical resemblance, but the tested abilities differ materially: PR-793 tests safe compliant interference insertion, while the candidate tests reversible adjustment locking and closed-loop commissioning from dynamic response. Candidate rebound, overload, drift, and tightening limits lack final numeric thresholds.
